new_matches.title: Senior TechOps Generalist
new_matches.description: Seen this advert before? That is because we are continuing to grow! We are very excited to be growing our small and efficient TechOps team at Octopus. We aren't looking for standard IT support - we are looking for an ambitious, deeply knowledgeable and experienced TechOps Generalist to join our team, to grow with the rest of the company, and ensure we are doing so in a secure and safe way. You will be a key partner in defining what TechOps is at Octopus. We will be continuing to shape this team to provide world class support to our employees, building our way out of problems with engineering firepower and undertaking transformational organisational change. We don't just "fix" things - we automate them out of existence. For us, a Generalist isn’t about knowing a little of everything, it’s a multi-disciplinary role for someone who’s deeply experienced in many facets of Enterprise IT. Think multi-domain specialist - not Jack of all trades. What is TechOps? A more modern, more lean version of a traditional Enterprise IT team with around one of us for every 1000 people at Octopus. We cover everything from what most people would call “1st line support” all the way up to high-level strategic planning, and everything in between. We tackle big problems and the breadth of work is huge. Dealing with ambiguity is a key part of working in TechOps, and every day will be a new and exciting one, working on varying challenges across the company and keeping plates spinning. We have a cloud-first approach to everything we do. This allows us to scale quickly and focus on things where we can add the most value. No on-prem AD here! Roles that you might currently be in: Systems engineer, DevOps, Tech support, Technical support, Technical support analyst, IT support, IT desktop support, Systems Administrator, Network Administrator, Workplace technology, Solutions specialist, Solutions administrator, Systems manager, Support manager. What you'll do Provide delightful day-to-day technical support to all areas of the business, to ensure our incredible employees are able to do their job as efficiently as possible. Their problems are our problems Troubleshoot and fix a wide range of technical issues, from laptop faults and network issues, to account provisioning failures and SSO problems Collaborate closely with our Security team to ensure we strike the right balance between security, productivity and user experience Continually find opportunities to automate our processes and improve the user experience Empower our people to help themselves by designing and building self-service solutions Monitor and maintain all the tech in our offices around the world - networks, meeting rooms, printers, digital signage, CCTV, door access control Managing supplier relationships and the procurement process for SaaS and hardware Lead and manage complex technical projects with multiple stakeholders from around the business. Examples of some TechOps projects include… Rollout of, and migration to, a new identity provider macOS and Windows MDM migration Rollout of a new device trust and posture compliance solution The replacement of insecure factors like SMS with phishing-resistant factors Office fit-outs, including tech like network, AV, access control etc SaaS migrations for acquisitions e.g. Microsoft 365 to Google Workspace What you'll need We’re looking for people with at least 5-7 years of solid enterprise IT experience. The technical bar is high. While we use Okta, Kandji, Kolide, Zscaler, Meraki and HiBob amongst others, we care about your understanding of the fundamentals of key SaaS tooling, but we also expect candidates to have significant experience implementing and customising these tools for Enterprise environments, so if you’ve lived in Entra and Intune? Awesome! You’ll also need: Confidence in articulating and implementing your technical ability, particularly with enterprise-level SaaS tooling, customer support and automation. The ability to do this both with your peers and novice users is vital A team player - we don’t want people who vanish and come back with perfect, completed work. You collaborate and work transparently and can identify who can help you, or needs your help Rich experience and examples of scripting, using APIs to automating mundane and error-prone repetitive tasks To be comfortable with a huge amount of ambiguity and spinning a lot of plates all at the same time Experience working with multiple teams and managing multiple stakeholders Experience managing and deploying macOS, Windows, iOS, and Android at scale Experience administering and troubleshooting Single Sign-On (SSO) technologies such as OAuth, OIDC and SAML Deep experience with Identity & Access Management. You should be able to explain the nuances of SAML, OIDC, and OAuth , and have hands-on experience with SCIM provisioning Experience of designing and installing office networks - we use Cisco Meraki A conscientious approach to everything you do and a passion for doing the right thing rather than the easy thing Don’t think you check off every single box? We love hiring passionate people with a drive to learn. If you are an expert in some of these areas and are hungry to master the rest, get in touch and let us know where your strengths lie. Why else you'll love it here Octopus Energy Group is a unique culture . An organisation where people learn, decide, and build quicker. Where people work with autonomy, alongside a wide range of amazing co-owners, on projects that break new ground. We want your hard work to be rewarded with perks you actually care about! We won best company to work for in 2022, on Glassdoor we were voted 50 best places to work in 2022 and our Group CEO, Greg has recorded a podcast about our culture and how we empower our people. We’ve also been placed in the top 10 companies for senior leadership Visit our UK perks hub - Octopus Employee Benefits This role can be either fully office based in any of our major offices in Brighton, Manchester, Leicester, Coventry or London , or a hybrid of a few days a week working remotely and office based. Our salary bandings are between £65,000 - £90,000 depending on your experience. On a call with one of our talent team, it's something we always chat through, as we genuinely want to match your experience with the right salary. We're very excited to be growing our small team. We're looking for skills and experience to help shape and define the future of not only our team, but the wider business at a global scale. If you're reading this and grinning, please apply! There are huge challenges to tackle, and we need amazing people who are keen to get stuck in. If this sounds like you then we'd love to hear from you. Are you ready for a career with us? We want to ensure you have all the tools and environment you need to unleash your potential. Need any specific accommodations? Whether you require specific accommodations or have a unique preference, let us know, and we'll do what we can to customise your interview process for comfort and maximum magic! Studies have shown that some groups of people, like women, are less likely to apply to a role unless they meet 100% of the job requirements. Whoever you are, if you like one of our jobs, we encourage you to apply as you might just be the candidate we hire. Across Octopus, we're looking for genuinely decent people who are honest and empathetic. Our people are our strongest asset and the unique skills and perspectives people bring to the team are the driving force of our success. As an equal opportunity employer, we do not discriminate on the basis of any protected attribute. Our commitment is to provide equal opportunities, an inclusive work environment, and fairness for everyone. Where necessary, we sometimes use AI tools to help with parts of our hiring process, like reviewing applications or assessing responses. We’re lucky to receive a huge amount of interest, so these tools help our recruiters manage that volume, not replace them. Ultimately, every hiring decision (for example, whether to progress your application or not) is always made by a real person in our Talent team. If you’d like to know more about how we use your data, you can reach out to us via email at talent@octoenergy.com. We’re happy to help!

new_matches.title: System Engineer
new_matches.description: Podium Advanced Technologies , con sede a Pont Saint Martin (Aosta), è una start up innovativa e consolidata, in forte espansione, leader nello sviluppo di tecnologie per il settore motorsport, prototipi e mobilità elettrica. Stiamo cercando un/una EE System Engineer che, a partire dai requisiti di progetto, sia in grado di definire, integrare e validare sistemi elettronici ed elettrici complessi, garantendo coerenza tra requisiti, architettura, sviluppo funzionale, interfacce HW/SW e attività di test. Il ruolo contribuisce alla realizzazione del prodotto attraverso attività di system engineering, integrazione con le altre discipline tecniche e collaborazione con fornitori, testing, validazione e Project Execution. Principali Responsabilità e Attività: Definizione e gestione dei requisiti di sistema EE, garantendone coerenza con i requisiti di progetto. Definizione e sviluppo dell’architettura di sistema EE, incluse le interfacce HW/SW. Gestione della suddivisione funzionale HW/SW e delle interfacce tra componenti. Sviluppo funzionale, integrazione e validazione dei sistemi elettronici ed elettrici. Definizione delle strategie di validazione, inclusi test plan e criteri di accettazione. Gestione della configurazione di sistema e allineamento con l’evoluzione del progetto. Verifica e supporto all’integrazione di sistema tramite simulazioni e test. Redazione e mantenimento della documentazione tecnica di sistema e documentazione di rilascio. Partecipazione alle attività di verifica, integrazione e delibera del sistema. Preparazione della documentazione tecnica per RFQ e supporto alla gestione tecnica dei fornitori. Collaborazione con team HW, SW, Control, E/E Design, Functional Safety e Project Chief per garantire la convergenza tecnica del sistema. Interfacciamento con il cliente. Requisiti: Laurea magistrale in Ingegneria Elettronica, dell’Informazione, Meccatronica, Automazione, Autoveicolo o discipline affini. Conoscenza dei processi di sviluppo di sistemi elettronici complessi in campo automotive o in alternativa ferroviario o avionico. Gradita conoscenza di normative e standard di settore, con particolare riferimento a processi di sviluppo, qualità, sicurezza funzionale e validazione. Gradita esperienza di almeno 2/3 anni in attività di system engineering, definizione requisiti, architetture elettrico/elettroniche Capacità di lavorare in team multidisciplinari e di interfacciarsi con fornitori e stakeholder di progetto. Buona conoscenza della lingua inglese. I nostri valori I nostri valori rappresentano la direzione. Le competenze e i comportamenti li rendono concreti. AMBIZIONE Visione, innovazione, orientamento al risultato. Puntiamo in alto e ci assumiamo la responsabilità di arrivarci. Non ci accontentiamo dello status quo e lavoriamo per trasformare problemi complessi in risultati concreti. FIDUCIA Integrità e correttezza relazionale. La fiducia si costruisce con la trasparenza. Significa dire le cose come stanno, affrontare i problemi e creare un contesto in cui il confronto è possibile. SOSTENIBILITÀ Immaginare e progettare il futuro. Costruiamo un’organizzazione che funziona nel tempo. Questo significa fare scelte anche difficili, evitare che i problemi si trascinino e progettare con responsabilità. LIBERTÀ Empowerment. Diamo spazio alle persone di incidere davvero. Autonomia e responsabilità vanno insieme: ognuno è chiamato a contribuire in modo attivo e consapevole. PASSIONE PER L’ECCELLENZA Capacità realizzativa e pensiero critico. Non ci basta fare. Vogliamo fare bene, migliorare continuamente e misurarci sui risultati. Cosa offriamo: CCNL Metalmeccanico, B1 RAL indicativa 33/38k Buoni pasto. Policy Smart Working. Flessibilità oraria. Programmi di welfare. Agevolazioni per il trasferimento in Valle d’Aosta.

new_matches.title: Lead Electrical Systems Engineer
new_matches.description: Job Description Summary GE Vernova’s Power Conversion & Storage (PCS) business provides electrification systems that are critical to customers’ power requirements for their high-performance, efficient and demanding applications. We work with the world’s major, industry, maritime and defence organisations, helping to enable a transition to energy efficiency, whilst delivering key capability, availability and decarbonisation through our advanced electrical power systems and marine power & propulsion solutions. The Marine Power Test Facility (MPTF) is a dedicated, full power, land-based test facility and plays a crucial role in de-risking present and future power and propulsion technologies, systems and from product development and verification through to complete, full-scale integrated power and propulsion including new ‘clean ship’ technologies. new_matches.title: Junior Platform Engineer
new_matches.description: Intric builds a sovereign AI platform for organisations that need to keep their data close: public-sector bodies, municipalities and critical infrastructure. It’s a small team, which means the work is real, the decisions matter and you’ll get close to the systems that actually keep the product running. As the second person on the platform team, you’ll work directly alongside the lead on day-to-day operations, investigations and larger infrastructure projects. This is an early-career role. You won’t be expected to arrive knowing the whole stack, but you will be expected to have solid foundations, learn quickly and take on more ownership as your understanding grows. The platform is largely self-hosted and open source. Kubernetes, k3s, Helm and Argo CD sit at the centre of it, alongside Docker and Dokploy environments that still need to be operated and migrated. Around that are Vault, Tailscale, Terraform, GitHub Actions, PostgreSQL, Redis, RabbitMQ, S3-compatible storage, Weaviate and a full OpenTelemetry and Grafana observability stack. Parts are sparsely documented and some of the problems won’t have a ready-made runbook. The learning curve is steep. What You’ll Do Get hands-on with the whole platform. Learn how our managed, dedicated and on-premises environments fit together. Make changes to Kubernetes manifests, Helm charts, Argo CD applications, Terraform and CI/CD workflows. Early changes will be scoped and reviewed closely; over time, you’ll be expected to drive routine work yourself. Take ownership of observability over time. Build a clear picture of what we can see across metrics, logs, traces, dashboards and alerts. Improve what’s missing, reduce noise and make incidents easier to understand. The stack includes OpenTelemetry, Grafana, Mimir, Loki and Tempo. Take on the day-to-day operational load. Triage alerts, investigate failing workloads, make routine configuration changes and verify that deployments and backups are doing what we expect. The goal is for you to handle documented and familiar issues without needing to escalate, while escalating unfamiliar or high-risk problems early. Turn repeated work into automation. If something has to be done twice, look for a way to make the third time safer and faster. That might mean a shell or Python script, a GitHub Actions workflow, a better alert or a proper runbook. Work across the application boundary. The workload is a Python and FastAPI backend with workers, RabbitMQ consumers and several stateful dependencies. You won’t be hired as a backend engineer, but you will learn enough about the application to follow a problem from ingress to API, queue, consumer and data store. Document what you learn. When the documentation runs out, go looking for the answer. Once you find it, leave the system clearer for the next person. Who you are You’re comfortable in a Linux environment and want to understand what the machine is actually doing. You understand the basics of processes, permissions, networking, DNS, HTTP and TLS. You don’t need to know everything from memory, but you need enough of a model to investigate when something breaks. You’ve used Git and Docker, and you can automate a small task in shell, Python or another scripting language. You approach problems methodically. You gather evidence, form a hypothesis, test it and explain what you found. You go looking for answers when the documentation runs out, but you don’t hide blockers or guess when the blast radius is large. You can move between investigations, operational work and implementation without losing track of what matters. You can fill in reasonable gaps in a brief yourself, while checking assumptions that could affect production. An infrastructure environment that isn’t built entirely around AWS or GCP managed services strikes you as more interesting, not more limiting. You might be a recent graduate or have built equivalent experience through projects, a homelab or early professional work. We care more about the foundations you have and how you learn than whether you already know our particular stack. Excellent communication skills are needed for this role because collaboration with the Forward Deployed Engineering and Product teams is part of the day to day work. What you don’t need You don’t need professional experience with every technology listed above. You don’t need to be a Kubernetes expert on your first day. You don’t need to have operated a production platform before. You do need to be curious, careful and ready to become independently useful faster than you would in a heavily layered engineering organisation. About Intric Europe's public sector is facing its biggest challenge in generations. A shrinking workforce must deliver more services to more people, and the gap grows every year. Intric exists to close it. We bring modern AI to the organisations that keep society running, and in doing so, we're defining how public services will work for decades to come. We value ownership, high standards, and thoughtful execution. Titles matter less than contribution. If you see something that can be improved, you take initiative. If something is unclear, you ask questions. If a customer faces a challenge, you lean in. We combine ambition with collaboration. We move fast, but we care deeply about doing things right. As we continue scaling across Europe, every team member plays a meaningful role in shaping both the company and the culture.

Wij bieden een leerzame omgeving waarin je je technische kennis kunt uitbreiden èn jezelf kunt certificeren. Zoek jij een springplank voor je verdere IT-carrière? Lees dan snel verder! Dit ga je doen Als Support Engineer bij PQR ben je verantwoordelijk voor het oplossen van incidenten bij onze klanten. Je handelt zowel eerste- als tweedelijns incidenten af, variërend van hardware- en softwarestoringen tot security-kwesties. Jij lost de storing zo efficiënt en klantvriendelijk mogelijk op! Daarbij werk je volgens de ITIL-methodiek en leg je contactmomenten vast in Autotask voor rapportage en terugkoppeling. We streven ernaar incidenten zo veel mogelijk binnen de Service Desk op te lossen, ‘first time fix’. Naast dat de gebruiker daar het meest mee geholpen is, leer je daar zelf ook veel van. Iedere klant met zijn eigen inrichting en technische uitdagingen, vraagt soms snel te schakelen en is in technisch opzicht hartstikke leerzaam. Naast dat we vanuit dit team de gebruikers zo optimaal mogelijk ondersteunen zijn we ook altijd bezig met het verbeteren van onze eigen processen. Op dit moment heeft het de efficiëntie van onze werkzaamheden en de inzet van AI daarbij, bijvoorbeeld voor het automatisch afhandelen van tickets of het onderhouden van werkinstructies, en “shift left” de aandacht. Ook daar draag jij als Support Engineer je steentje aan bij! Vanuit de Service Desk zijn we het eerste aanspreekpunt voor incidenten en verstoringen voor ongeveer 130 klanten die het IT beheer aan PQR uitbesteed hebben. De Service Desk is onderdeel van PQR Managed Services. Binnen onze Managed Service organisatie richten we ons zoveel mogelijk op het voorkomen van incidenten. Mocht zich dan toch een incident voordoen, dan proberen we het zo op te lossen dat het incident zich niet meer herhaalt. Zo blijven we Rustmakers in IT. Vereisten Uiteraard Ben Je Communicatief Vaardig En Beschik Je Over Uitstekende Probleem Oplossende Vaardigheden. Je Bent Leergierig En In Staat Snel Te Schakelen Tussen Verschillende Omgevingen En Type Problemen. Daarnaast Vragen Wij Ervaring in het ondersteunen van gebruikers; Interesse in AI en hoe je dit in je werk kan inzetten om je werkzaamheden te optimaliseren; Gedegen kennis van Active directory, Microsoft Office producten, Windows besturingssystemen en M365; Kennis van ITIL processen en ITSM; Je beschikt over de MS100, MD102, AZ900 en ITIL certificering, of enthousiasme om deze te behalen; Ervaring met Citrix (Netscaler, Virtual Apps & Desktop) en/of netwerk kennis is een pré; Je bent bereid om flexibel te werken binnen de openingstijden van de Service Desk, van 06:00 tot 20:00 uur. De diensten zijn verdeeld over verschillende werktijden: van 06:00 tot 14:30 uur (thuiswerken), van 08:00 tot 16:30 uur (op kantoor) en van 11:30 tot 20:00 uur (thuiswerken); Als echte rustmaker kan jij je helemaal vinden in een proactieve aanpak en denk je mee over standaardisatie en structuur! Mocht je nog stappen te zetten hebben, maar jezelf wel grotendeels herkennen in deze functie? Laat je gegevens achter en dan bespreken we de mogelijkheden met jou. Dit bieden wij je Samenwerken met professionals op hoog kennisniveau en een grote mate van zelfstandigheid; Uitstekende opleidingsmogelijkheden vanuit onze Spacehub Academy, een buddy om jezelf te ontwikkelen en we ondersteunen je in het behalen van certificeringen; Regelmatig georganiseerde trainingen, kennissessies en gezellige borrels; Uitstekende primaire- en secundaire arbeidsvoorwaarden, inclusief laptop, mobiele telefoon. Over PQR Bij PQR werk je bij dé marktleider op het gebied van geavanceerde IT-infrastructuren. We zijn trots op onze hoge partner statussen en bieden volop kansen om jezelf te ontwikkelen en door te groeien binnen PQR en/of ons moederbedrijf Bechtle. Met onze kennis helpen we klanten om rust te brengen in hun IT-omgeving. Onze klanten zijn o.a. actief in de zorg, gemeenten, semi-overheid, en transport. Waarom jij deze uitdaging elke dag bij ons aangaat? Simpelweg omdat wij een hecht team hebben waarin iedereen de samenwerking met collega’s opzoekt, we kennis delen en opbouwen met elkaar en op vrijdagmiddag staan jouw collega's klaar voor de gezellige vrijdagmiddagborrel! Dit alles kan natuurlijk niet zonder de lekkerste koffies, dagelijks vers fruit, jaarlijks diverse feesten en events, teamuitje en nog veel meer. Geïnteresseerd? Ben jij de teamspeler die graag gebruikers en collega’s ondersteunt in het oplossen van technische problemen? En wil je ook jezelf als engineer verder ontwikkelen? Dan willen we je graag spreken! Reageer direct en we vertellen je alles over ons PQR-team, hoe we samenwerken aan de meest slimme IT-oplossingen voor de mooiste klanten en wat PQR voor jou kan betekenen.

About In-Person Giving At Fundraise Up In-Person Giving brings the quality and connected data of Fundraise Up’s online donation experience into physical fundraising moments. The product begins with Tap to Donate and Giving Station: staff-led and self-service experiences that let nonprofits accept contactless donations at events, in public spaces, and through other offline workflows. Every transaction should connect to the same campaigns, donor records, reporting, CRM integrations, and operational controls used across Fundraise Up. The next product direction is Events & Commerce . It includes ticket sales, check-in, merchandise and food purchases, symbolic purchases, auctions, paddle raises, and additional donations before and during an event. These capabilities must work as one connected fundraising system rather than another isolated event tool. About The Role We are hiring a Product Manager to own Events & Commerce within the broader In-Person Giving product line. This is a hands-on software product role covering discovery, definition, delivery, launch, and iteration. You will turn a large category into a focused product direction grounded in customer workflows, live usage, and commercial evidence. You will work closely with the PM responsible for the broader In-Person Giving area so that event commerce builds on the same payment, campaign, donor-data, reporting, mobile, and operational foundations as Tap to Donate and Giving Station. You will also partner with the Peer-to-Peer team where ticketing and event capabilities should be shared rather than rebuilt separately. This is not an event-planning, sales, or internal project-coordination role. What You’ll Own Define the product direction Turn customer research, market evidence, and business context into a clear Events & Commerce product thesis and sequenced roadmap. Choose a focused target segment and event scenario rather than trying to replace every event platform at once. Decide which capabilities belong in the shared In-Person Giving foundation and which require an Events-specific model. Make explicit decisions about what Fundraise Up should build, integrate, partner on, or deliberately exclude. Keep assumptions, success metrics, scope, risks, and product decisions visible. Lead discovery and product definition Work directly with nonprofit fundraising teams, event operators, finance teams, volunteers, attendees, donors, design partners, and internal GTM teams. Map the complete workflow before, during, and after an event—including purchase, donation, check-in, fulfillment, reconciliation, reporting, and follow-up. Validate decisions through interviews, workflow observation, prototypes, and live product usage. Separate true adoption blockers from feature requests and expectations created by incumbent event platforms. Shape problems such as ticket sales, QR-based check-in, guest management, commerce catalogues, FMV and receipts, on-site purchases, auctions, paddle raises, refunds, attribution, reporting, and integrations. These are examples—not a pre-committed feature checklist. Shape and deliver the product Own the product from problem definition through requirements, delivery, launch, and iteration. Write clear requirements, acceptance criteria, edge cases, state transitions, and decision records. Make day-to-day scope and trade-off decisions with Engineering, Design, Analytics, Research, QA, and GTM partners. Design for real event conditions: staff and volunteer operators, self-service flows, mobile devices, optional hardware, unreliable connectivity, high-volume moments, and operational recovery. Ensure that event capabilities reuse Fundraise Up’s existing payments, campaign, donor, reporting, CRM, and identity infrastructure wherever possible. Keep delivery predictable by surfacing dependencies, risks, and unresolved decisions early. Launch, learn, and drive outcomes Launch through EAPs with clear entry criteria, target workflows, success measures, readiness requirements, and out-of-scope areas. Understand whether organizations can configure and run the target event workflows without heavy manual work or disconnected tools. Measure whether attendees can purchase, check in, donate, and receive the right confirmation or receipt through a clear experience. Partner with Product Marketing, Sales, CSM, Support, Finance, Legal, and Operations on positioning, commitments, enablement, and launch readiness. Connect product evidence to activation, adoption, event completion, GPV, expansion, pipeline, retention, and operational cost. Turn evidence into explicit recommendations: iterate, expand, change direction, partner, or stop. Work AI-native Use AI for research synthesis, workflow analysis, prototyping, specification quality, data exploration, and operational automation. Build testable artifacts quickly without outsourcing product judgment. Requirements 4–7 years of Product Management or Product Ownership experience in a software product company. End-to-end ownership of a customer-facing product area with Engineering and Design. Strong judgment in reducing a large problem space to a focused release and explaining the trade-offs. Experience turning customer evidence and product data into decisions. Clear written communication across requirements, edge cases, metrics, and decision records. Ability to work with transactional, multi-actor workflows involving permissions, states, money, and data relationships. High ownership and independence, with fluent written and spoken English. Strong plus Experience with ticketing, event technology, commerce, POS, payments, marketplaces, registration, auctions, or other transaction-heavy products. Experience with mobile applications, contactless payments, physical devices, or hardware-enabled workflows. Experience with B2B SaaS, fundraising, nonprofits, or other operationally complex customer environments. Experience launching a new product area through beta or EAP. Knowledge of CRM integrations, financial reconciliation, reporting, transaction attribution, analytics, or SQL. Practical use of AI for research, prototyping, analysis, or product operations. This Role May Not Be a Fit If You are looking for an event-planning or internal project-management role rather than software product ownership. You prefer to receive a fully defined roadmap and requirements instead of helping determine what should be built. You want to work only on strategy and avoid specifications, QA, delivery details, or post-launch iteration. You treat every customer request as a roadmap commitment. You need stable scope and certainty before moving forward. You measure progress mainly by features shipped rather than customer and business outcomes. Why work with us Build a new product direction from research through live customer use. Work in a large, proven fundraising category with clear customer demand and meaningful commercial potential. Shape ticketing and event commerce as part of a broader fundraising platform rather than an isolated event tool. Work with real nonprofit customers, rich product evidence, and experienced cross-functional partners. Join a small team where product managers have meaningful ownership and direct access to Product leadership. Help define an AI-native approach to product management in practice. new_matches.description: Job Description The Commander has the whole responsibility and Authority for the safe conduct of the flight, and the safety of the crew, the airplane, its cargo, and its supernumeraries. He must comply with the standing regulations and clearances received from the competent authorities. He maintains familiarity with relevant Maltese and international air legislation and agreed aviation practices and procedures. The Commander is the representative of CAC on-board the aircraft; the entire crew is at all times under the Commander's Authority. This Authority extends in addition to the whole of the crew duty period, including the stay away from the home base. The Commander is responsible and has the Authority with regard to the behavior, appearance and location of the entire crew during the whole duration of the crew's assignment. Not undertake duties for any other operator, without prior approval from the Flight Operations Manager. All FTLs must be respected in regard to Flight Duty Periods with all operators where duties are undertaken. The Commander ensures that operations are conducted in accordance with any restriction on the routes or the areas of operation specified by the competent authority. He conducts a crew briefing, relating information and particulars pertinent to the individual flight. The Commander shall, as soon as possible, report to the appropriate air traffic services (ATS) unit any hazardous weather or flight conditions encountered that are likely to affect the safety of other aircraft. Responsibilities Comply with the Operations Manual. Determine and confirm aircraft airworthiness prior to flight, including review of ATL, MEL and CDL, ensuring required inspections are completed, aircraft configuration complies with CDL, and required instruments and equipment are serviceable except as permitted by MEL/CDL. Ensure all known or suspected defects are recorded in the ATL and that no flight departs unless defects affecting airworthiness are properly processed in accordance with MEL/CDL, and associated operational procedures are followed. Decide on acceptance or rejection of an aircraft with unserviceable items in accordance with MEL/CDL (OM‑B Ch. 8 & 9), with authority to reject the aircraft if dissatisfied with airworthiness or maintenance status. Ensure preflight inspections are completed in accordance with OM‑B Ch. 2, including exterior and interior inspections covering critical surfaces, controls, systems, emergency equipment, and structural integrity. Ensure required fuel, mass and balance, and aircraft performance are sufficient for safe completion of the planned flight, and that documentation is correctly completed and retained. Be responsible for the safety of the aircraft, crew, supernumeraries and cargo from arrival onboard until leaving the aircraft, and from commencement of taxi until engines are shut down at flight completion. Exercise full authority to issue commands and take necessary actions to ensure safety, including disembarkation of persons or cargo posing a safety risk, refusal of intoxicated persons (except medical cases), and refusal of inadmissible supernumeraries or persons in custody when safety is compromised. Ensure supernumeraries are briefed on emergency exits and safety equipment, that cabins, galleys, exits and escape paths are secured and unobstructed, and emergency equipment is accessible. Ensure all operational procedures, checklists and critical phase restrictions are complied with. Ensure flight recorders are not disabled, erased or improperly handled, and are preserved following occurrences, serious incidents or accidents in accordance with applicable regulations. Prior to take‑off, ensure weather, runway condition and aerodrome operating minima permit a safe departure. Ensure crew and supernumeraries are properly secured before take‑off and landing. Ensure required documents and manuals are carried, valid and available throughout the flight. Utilize the company safety reporting system in accordance with Chapter 11. Maintain a high standard of discipline, conduct and professional appearance as a representative of CAC. Education To be employed by CAC as Commander the candidate shall fulfill as minimum: Holds a valid EASA Airline Transport Pilots License in accordance with Commission Regulation (EU) No. 1178/2011; Medical Certificate Class I; Holds a valid Instrument Rating (IR); 5.000 hrs total time; If Type Rated: 2.000 hours PIC on a medium/heavy jet; 500 hrs on type as Commander or Boeing Heavy Jet. If Non-Type Rated: 6.000 hours total time; 3.000 hours PIC on a medium/heavy jet. Experience Minimum experience levels may be lowered by the NP Flight Operations in consultation and agreement with the NP Crew Training based on the quality of the Crew Members experience (e.g.: long haul vs. short haul, actual stick time vs augmented crew time). If the experience levels are lowered for a particular candidate this should be agreed upon by the NP Flight Operations and NP Crew Training and then documented with the Compliance Monitoring Manager.

The role will require to maintain a healthy and professional relationship with arbitration bodies, contribute to root cause analysis, and actively participate in shaping future policies and operational decisions within the complaints team. The role demands diligence, legal acumen, consistency, and the ability to handle sensitive information with the utmost care. Conduct audits on the internal handling of the Customer complaint journey, ensuring a fair outcome. Arbitration decision process: Assess cases and decisions made by the arbitration body, taking responsibility for the legally binding decision. Complaint Market & Regulatory Expertise: Maintain an in-depth understanding of local regulatory frameworks, evolving arbitration body assessments, and the unique differences in jurisdictional complaints, ensuring compliance and optimal outcomes for Wise and its customers in the global market. Proactively monitor regulatory changes and interpret their impact on our customers and processes. Mitigate reputational damage from adverse decisions: Defend Wise against adverse decisions to safeguard the company's reputation. Work across multiple teams: Communicate with relevant product/operational teams to ensure a comprehensive understanding of cases and the ability to articulate this information to the arbitration body. Consistently hitting SLAs: Consistently handling cases within Wise’s SLAs, as well ensuring we do not breach cases based on the arbitration body deadline. Strong Fincrime knowledge: Maintain up-to-date knowledge on scam and deactivation complaints, understanding how they are handled across the business. Communication: You’re a great communicator. You welcome an open feedback culture, happy both giving and receiving feedback to or from anyone in the organization, and you can adapt to Wise's style of communication. Analytical Mindset: You are comfortable working with data, noticing patterns, trends, and systemic issues to draw meaningful conclusions. Tooling & BI: You have a good command of Lightdash, Looker, SQL, or other Business Intelligence (BI) tools. You actively look for incremental improvements, aiming to streamline workflows, eliminate non-value-adding steps, and uncover root causes rather than treating surface symptoms. You are familiar with problem-solving frameworks (e.g., 5 Whys, Fishbone diagrams) or are eager to learn them. Organization & Autonomy: You are punctual, highly organized, and efficient at prioritizing your workload under pressure. You operate autonomously, taking confident ownership of decisions on complex cases while managing your time and energy effectively. Reliability & Adaptability: You display strong commitment to team goals, adapt quickly to regulatory shift, and consistently follow through on commitments. Regulatory Understanding & Security: You have a solid grasp of European regulatory frameworks (or a strong willingness to learn), and you consistently uphold strict data protection and security procedures. Customer Focus: Our customers come first and we make no compromises on that—you consistently keep the customer’s best interest at heart, ensuring fair treatment across all arbitration cases. new_matches.title: Senior Infrastructure and Data Engineer (Remote in Europe)
new_matches.description: About the role Hyperion Quantitative Strategies is an AI-native systematic fund built end to end by its own engineering team. Kubernetes on Google Cloud, Terraform-managed infrastructure, automated pipelines pulling market data across equities, options, index options, volatility and crypto at minute and daily resolution, a proprietary backtesting engine, and a live trading book. The fund is already in discussions that would take it to several hundred million dollars in assets under management, and the ambition is a firm built in the spirit of Renaissance Technologies, with AI core to how it operates rather than a layer sitting on top. The engineering bench is deliberately small and senior. One engineer deep in backtesting and infrastructure, one in agentic systems and the data lake, one in data engineering — and the CTO owning the quantitative layer above them. This role sits across the whole platform: cloud architecture, data pipelines, production reliability and live-system ownership, in one senior individual contributor seat. Infrastructure is the floor, not the ceiling. You design the systems, you run them, and the calls about where the platform goes next are yours to make. You will report directly to the CTO and co-founder. Copenhagen is the preferred base; strong candidates in CET-compatible European time zones are considered. Hyperion is built inside the Bifrost Studios portfolio, and Bifrost Studios is running this search. What you'll do Own and evolve the Kubernetes platform on Google Cloud (GKE) through Terraform, with infrastructure as code treated as an engineering discipline rather than a collection of scripts. Build and operate the pipelines that ingest market data from multiple vendors — normalisation, validation and strict format compliance included — so the trading engine always has numbers it can rely on. Own deployment, monitoring, alerting and incident response for the live trading systems, so problems in the running book surface early and get resolved fast. Own the relational and analytical databases behind trading and research: schema design, performance, operations, and fault-tolerant, high-availability architecture where it earns its place. Steward the integrations with external data providers and broker connectivity, and treat the proprietary data as a long-term asset — a number pulled two years from now should still be safe to trade on. Cut operational toil through automation, so the platform needs progressively less manual intervention as it matures. Work directly alongside the CTO and the quant and data engineering team, acting as the clear owner the moment something breaks during market hours. Twelve months in, success looks like this: the research and quant team has stopped thinking about infrastructure because it just stays reliable. What we're looking for End-to-end production ownership. You have owned a production infrastructure and data platform somewhere reliability genuinely mattered — not a narrow slice of a large platform team, and not consuming infrastructure somebody else ran. This is the filter. It typically shows up somewhere between five and twelve years in, but we do not filter on years. Kubernetes, GCP and Terraform in production , with infrastructure as code held as an engineering discipline. A track record of building reliable, automated pipelines from messy external sources , with real familiarity with vendor quirks, corporate actions, adjustments and timezone handling. Strong Python and Java. JavaScript is welcome. Solid relational database skills across schema design, performance and operations, plus DevOps depth: CI/CD, observability, on-call practice and fault-tolerant architecture. Genuinely AI-native. You use AI coding agents as standard practice, not as something you are warming up to, and you can explain every line that ships and what it does to the system. A real interest in markets. Prior experience with trading or market data systems is a meaningful plus. A finance background is not required. Based in Copenhagen or within a CET-compatible European time zone. About Bifrost Studios Bifrost Studios builds and backs ambitious technology businesses, providing portfolio companies with the operational, engineering and sourcing infrastructure to grow with intent. Hyperion Quantitative Strategies is one of those businesses — and this search is being run directly by the Bifrost Studios team on Hyperion's behalf. If you are a senior engineer who wants full ownership of a live, consequential platform at the earliest stage where the decisions you make now are the ones it runs on for years, we would like to hear from you. Process: Intro call with the recruiter → technical deep dive with the CTO → interview with the quant and engineering team → case assessment and psychometrics → references and offer. Copenhagen, Denmark — CET-compatible European time zones considered. Full-time employee.
